footage.hint.hevc: HEVC (H.265) can usually be decoded by Safari on a Mac and by Chrome or Edge on Windows and macOS. Chrome on Linux needs hardware decoding.

footage.browser.no_avc: This browser cannot encode H.264 video. Please use a current Chrome, Edge or Safari.
footage.browser.no_opfs: This browser cannot store files temporarily (private window?). Please use a normal window of Chrome, Edge or Safari.
footage.browser.no_aac: This browser cannot encode AAC sound. Clips whose sound is already AAC at 48 kHz still work; other clips are reported as failed.

export.title: Export · {cut}
export.lead: A package for your editing application that points straight to the original files on your computer. You render there.
export.no_cut: There is no cut yet. The export becomes available as soon as the first cut is ready.
export.where.title: 1 · Where is the footage?
export.root: Path of the folder “{folder}” on your computer
export.root.hint: In Explorer: right-click the folder → “Copy as path”. In Finder: select the folder, press ⌥⌘C.
export.root.mismatch: The path ends in “{path}”, but you chose the folder “{folder}”. Please check that both are the same folder.
export.check.title: 2 · Check the originals
export.check.lead: Nothing is uploaded. Your browser compares the name, size and fingerprint of every file with what was uploaded.
export.check.skip: You can export without the check; then every clip is expected at its old place.

export.error.failed: The package could not be made: {message}
export.error.format: This format is not available yet.
export.error.root: Please enter the path of the footage folder.
export.readme.premiere.title: {title}, {cut} – import into Premiere Pro
export.readme.where: These files belong in the folder {folder} (the subfolder _cutlery of your footage folder). The timeline finds your original clips, the music, the titles and the maps from there.
export.readme.premiere.steps:
1. In Premiere Pro: File → Import, choose {timeline}. A new sequence appears in the project.
2. If clips appear offline: right-click → Link Media, select the first missing clip in your footage folder; Premiere finds the others.
3. Subtitles: File → Import, choose {srt}, drag it onto the sequence as a caption track.
4. Titles are PNG pictures on their own video track; replace them with your own titles if you like.
5. Render the film from the sequence (File → Export → Media).
export.readme.not_included: Not included and marked instead (markers on the sequence): stabilisation and audio cleanup of single shots, and the decisions from the review.
